confirmed: The source is arXiv:2602.10001v3 [cs.SI], dated 14 Jul 2026, with eight PDF pages. The title and seven authors match the form. The entire markdown and PDF were read; the document ends with references and contains no appendix or stated supplement (PDF p. 1, title/byline/version banner; pp. 7-8, Acknowledgments and References).

The main experiment includes humans receiving indirect AI-generated hints, so it is not solely an AI-versus-human-output study. However, the explicit randomization assigns hybrid-game rounds to human or Gemini players; allocation of people across Human Social, Human Asocial, and Human-AI Hybrid is unstated. Thus S1 design_class = other, assignment.randomized = not_stated, criterion 1/core = unclear, and context_class = none are defensible. The false checker flag means no documented randomized-people study was confirmed, not that nonrandom assignment was established (PDF p. 3, Experimental conditions).

The PDF reports 503 successfully recruited people and condition sample sizes of 210 Human Social, 179 Human Asocial, and 114 Human-AI Hybrid. These are people, not games, guesses, API calls, or ratings; separate assignment and post-exclusion counts are not reported (PDF p. 3, Experimental conditions and Human participants).

Each game has 10 rounds with 10 guesses per round, and similarity feedback uses Word2Vec cosine similarity scaled by 201.69. Human Social players contribute one round per game in up to 10 games; Human Asocial players complete one entire game; Hybrid humans contribute one round per game and are described as participating in 10 games (PDF p. 3, Method and Experimental conditions).

The assistance is indirect best-guess information from other players, including Gemini agents in hybrid games; humans are not told that guesses may have come from AI. Gemini 2.5 Flash is identified as the June 17, 2025 release, at temperature 0.7 (PDF p. 3, Experimental conditions and AI queries).

S1-O1 correctly reports Human-AI Hybrid performance M = 87.76. The results text gives p < .001 against the other conditions, whereas the Human Social-versus-Hybrid bracket in Figure 3A has ** and the caption defines the 0.01 significance level. No numerical Human Social mean is printed (PDF pp. 3-4, Performance analysis; p. 5, Figure 3A/caption and Controlling for effect of model type and synergy).

S1-O2 correctly reports collective Hybrid lexical diversity M = 0.58, below the human conditions; the measure combines human and AI guesses in hybrid games. It is an average of within-game proportions of unique words, distinct from the human-only comparison in Figure 4B (PDF p. 4, Diversity analysis; p. 5, Figures 3C and 4B).

S1-O3 and the one-line finding correctly report no significant human-performance difference between Hybrid and Human Social: p = 0.392, d = 0.032. The one-line Hybrid mean M = 87.76 is also printed. Numerical human-subgroup means are not supplied (PDF p. 5, Interaction with people changes AI behavior, Figure 4A, and Controlling for effect of model type and synergy).

The outcomes are computed on produced guesses: round-maximum target similarity and lexical word uniqueness. The convergent-task designation and the caveat that collective Hybrid outcomes include AI outputs are supported; these are not self-reported creativity measures (PDF pp. 3-4, Performance analysis and Diversity analysis; p. 6, Discussion limitations).

S2 is a model-only control using Gemini 2.5 Flash, GPT 5.1, and a 50%/50% mixture, reusing the original human-hybrid comparison. GPT 5.1 uses temperature 0.7 and medium reasoning effort; the new control conditions add no human sample (PDF p. 3, AI queries; pp. 5-6, Controlling for effect of model type and synergy).

S3 and S4 are explicitly AI-only controls. Communication variants are Complete History, Short Advice, and Long Advice; temperature variants are 0.3, 0.5, 0.9, and 1.1 relative to the main 0.7 setting. None establishes randomized human assistance (PDF p. 3, AI queries; p. 6, Controlling for prompts and social information).

This is an original experimental paper, not a review or meta-analysis; leaving synthesis counts and pooled-estimate fields at their defaults is appropriate (PDF pp. 3-6, Method, Results, and control experiments).
summary: The form's version and headline numbers match the v3 PDF, but it omits the human-specific diversity result and leaves comparison details incomplete. Random assignment of people is unreported, and the 503 recruited participants should not be presented as a confirmed analyzed count.
